card.name: Word "you" in website prompts
card.fires_on: The word "you" in reader-prompt phrases on web pages, mainly "What made you want to look up..." and "Did you find this article useful?". It also fires weakly on past-tense verbs like "were not" or "There was".

modes.label: Dictionary look-up prompt
modes.description: "you" right after "What made" in an encyclopedia-style look-up question.
modes.example: What made<< you>> want to look up "tenor drum

modes.label: Article feedback prompt
modes.description: "you" after "Did" in a request for reader feedback.
modes.example: Did<< you>> find this article useful? Send comments and

modes.label: Past-tense statements
modes.description: A weaker response on past-tense verbs or negations that describe how things used to be.
modes.example: Trampolines were<< not>> designed to be backyard toys.

card.writes: It promotes words meaning "previously" or "originally" and suppresses words meaning "currently", so it pushes toward past-time wording.
card.plain: It fires on "you" in website questions like "What made you want to look up..." and nudges the next words toward past-time wording.
